biography.heading: A Life Devoted to the Canvas
biography.intro: Ako Gharib has spent a lifetime translating the memory, struggle, and humor of the Kurdish people into paint.
paragraphs: Born into a land shaped by mountains and migration, Ako Gharib first learned to draw before he learned to write — sketching the faces of elders, the folds of traditional dress, and the silhouettes of a homeland often contested but never forgotten.

His historical and national works trace the long arc of Kurdish identity: uprisings and quiet resilience, festivals and exile, rendered with the reverence of a chronicler and the hand of a painter trained in classical realism.
Alongside this, a sharper, wittier line runs through his political caricatures — a decades-long conversation with power, drawn with humor sharp enough to disarm and honest enough to sting.
In his portraits, the two impulses meet: every subject, famous or unnamed, is painted as history in progress — a face worth remembering.
biography.quote: A brush is the quietest way to raise your voice.
